subject: QuellTech inference event — after-action dossier and corrective roadmap
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@quelltech.com>

Cc: Ava Li <ava.li@quelltech.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike 5/9-5/10 — latency + 5xx surge (examples attached)

Diego / Redwood team,

We observed a sharp degradation in inference performance yesterday evening (PDT). Key symptoms:
- P50 latency increased from ~200ms to ~1.8s for our chat route between 22:30-23:15 PDT.
- Error rate (5xx) jumped from ~0.2% baseline to ~6% during the same window.
- Sustained throughput drop on our dedicated pool despite steady request volume.

I've attached a short log excerpt showing repeated KV-cache misses and multiple model-variant fallbacks. This is production-impacting for our customer-facing flows. Please advise:
1) Can you confirm receipt and an initial cause hypothesis?
2) What immediate mitigations can we expect and ETA?
3) We will need a timeline for a full write-up and proposed corrective actions for our execs.

Attached: quell_incident_log_excerpt.txt

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Production Ops, QuellTech

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: QuellTech throughput event — immediate mitigations and ownership

Team — quick internal plan from the triage bridge:
Summary: QuellTech saw increased latency and 5xxs correlated with a deployment that changed KV-cache keys and temporarily reduced effective batching. The runtime started routing to a larger, slower model variant under load which amplified latency.
Immediate mitigations (owners / ETA):
- Revert the KV-key change for the affected route (karthik) — ETA 30m.
- Force routing to the smaller low-latency variant for the next 6 hours (monica) — ETA 15m.
- Increase dedicated pool instances by +20% to prevent throttle-induced fallbacks (infra ops + karthik) — ETA 45m.
- Deploy a short-lived prefix cache that preserves hot prefixes (neha) — ETA 2 hours.
- Prepare an external exec one-pager and a credits proposal (markus) — ETA 4 hours.

Please confirm ownership inline. I'll draft the external message for Samir after owners confirm. Attaching a working corrective roadmap for tracking.

Attachment: corrective-roadmap-qtr2.pdf

Thanks,
Diego

Subject: Re: Spike 5/9-5/10 — latency + 5xx surge (examples attached)

Samir / Ava — quick update and commitments.

What we did (within first 2 hours):
- Reverted the KV key change that caused cache churn (karthik).
- Pinned your chat route to the low-latency model variant for 6 hours and added +20% pool capacity (monica / infra).
- Rolled a short-lived prefix cache for hot keys to reduce repeated cold-start overhead (neha).

Impact observed:
- Error rate returned to baseline within ~45 minutes of the revert.
- P50 latency returned to ~220ms for the pinned route; small tail improvements expected as caches warm.

Next deliverables:
- Internal corrective roadmap and ownership ledger (attached).
- Exec one-pager + SLA credits proposal (markus leading) — delivery by EOD today.
- Full incident write-up with timeline and root-cause analysis in JIRA-QT-245 — delivery within 72 hours.

Please confirm if you want us to proceed with the planned credit via DocuSign; Markus will reach out with the proposed amount. Also, if you can share two representative request IDs from the event window, we'll include request-level trace correlation in the write-up.

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@quelltech.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Closure: QuellTech 5/9-5/10 event — root cause, fixes, and follow-through

Samir / team — closing note with full summary and next steps.
Root cause (summary):
- The immediate cause was KV-cache key schema changes deployed to a routing micro-service which produced high cache-miss rates on hot prefixes. That increased backend work and caused the runtime to fall back to a larger model variant under sustained load.
- Contributing factors: insufficient canary coverage for the key-schema change and a missing pre-deployment load validation for routing config.

Corrective actions completed:
- Reverted key-schema change and restored stable cache behavior.
- Implemented a temporary routing pin to low-latency variant while we validate changes.
- Deployed a controlled prefix caching strategy and monitored heatmap for 72 hours.
- Increased dedicated pool headroom and adjusted autoscaling thresholds to reduce fallback probability.

Process changes (near-term):
- Add an automated pre-deploy traffic validation for routing and key-schema changes (owner: engineering infra).
- Canary policy update: expand canary traffic to 1% and run a 30-minute window of load tests for routing changes (owner: platform QA).
- Add a runbook entry for immediate checklist when fallback to variant occurs with >1% error deltas (owner: ops runbooks).

Customer remediation:
- We applied a one-time credit (proposal sent via DocuSign link) to the account as discussed.
- Monitoring: 14-day elevated observability retention for QuellTech routes to validate stability.

Attachments: post-incident-summary.html (includes timeline, annotated logs, and action tracker).
JIRA ticket: JIRA-QT-245 (incident write-up and action items).

Ask: Please confirm closure from QuellTech execs so we can move items 2 & 3 from "in progress" to "complete". Happy to walk through the one-pager in your exec sync if helpful.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
